title: 3801. Minimum Cost to Merge Sorted Lists

examples.explanation: Merge a = [1, 3, 5] and b = [2, 4]: len(a) = 3 and len(b) = 2 median(a) = 3 and median(b) = 2 cost = len(a) + len(b) + abs(median(a) - median(b)) = 3 + 2 + abs(3 - 2) = 6 So lists becomes [[1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8]]. Merge a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] and b = [6, 7, 8]: len(a) = 5 and len(b) = 3 median(a) = 3 and median(b) = 7 cost = len(a) + len(b) + abs(median(a) - median(b)) = 5 + 3 + abs(3 - 7) = 12 So lists becomes [[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]], and total cost is 6 + 12 = 18.

Merge a = [1, 1, 5] and b = [1, 4, 7, 8]: len(a) = 3 and len(b) = 4 median(a) = 1 and median(b) = 4 cost = len(a) + len(b) + abs(median(a) - median(b)) = 3 + 4 + abs(1 - 4) = 10 So lists becomes [[1, 1, 1, 4, 5, 7, 8]], and total cost is 10.

Merge a = [1] and b = [3]: len(a) = 1 and len(b) = 1 median(a) = 1 and median(b) = 3 cost = len(a) + len(b) + abs(median(a) - median(b)) = 1 + 1 + abs(1 - 3) = 4 So lists becomes [[1, 3]], and total cost is 4.
The total cost is len(a) + len(b) + abs(median(a) - median(b)) = 1 + 1 + abs(1 - 1) = 2.
